content.comment_body: Hello, I installed Windows 7 on my laptop and set up Windows XP Service Pack 3 as a virtual machine. After that, I installed [product_name] V6 in XP mode and upgraded to [product_name] V7. When I try to connect the PC to [product_name], I receive the following error: interface specified not available. Please check: correct connection mode, PC with [product_name], and correct interface selection. I have checked everything, but it still doesn’t work.
Hi, I suspect the drivers are not installed correctly. Try installing directly on Windows 7 using this link: [url].
Hello, [product_name] V6 will not install on Windows 7. How can I upgrade to V7 if I don't have the main version installed on Windows 7?

The instructions are all there in the link I provided. Begin installing V7; the software will prompt you for the location of the previous version. Navigate to the CD or directory where your full V6 version is located and follow the steps in the link.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are having trouble connecting their PC to [product_name] after installing [product_name] in a virtual Windows XP environment running on Windows 7. The main challenge involves compatibility and upgrade issues between software versions and operating systems, particularly from V6 to V7, and ensuring the correct drivers are installed. Despite checking the recommended troubleshooting steps, a connection error persists.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect to install, upgrade, and operate [product_name] smoothly on their PC’s current operating system and reliably connect to [product_name] without encountering installation or driver issues.
